name: NE555DR
title: NA555, NE555, SA555, SE555 precision timers
summary: Single 555 timer for monostable delays and astable oscillation, from microseconds to hours, set by external resistors and a capacitor. Threshold and trigger levels sit at two thirds and one third of VCC and can be moved through CONT. The output sinks or sources up to 200 mA. Four temperature grades: NE555 0 °C to 70 °C, SA555 -40 °C to 85 °C, NA555 -40 °C to 105 °C, SE555 -55 °C to 125 °C; NE555DR is the NE555 in an 8-pin SOIC on a 2500-piece reel.

circuits.title: Circuit for monostable operation
circuits.description: One-shot pulse generator. A low-going edge at the input takes TRIG under one third of VCC; the output goes high and the discharge switch opens, so C charges through RA. At two thirds of VCC the threshold comparator ends the pulse: the output drops and DISCH empties C. The pulse lasts about 1.1 × RA × C. RESET is held at VCC, CONT is bypassed to ground, and RL is the load from VCC to the output.
notes: Typical monostable waveforms are given for RA = 9.1 kΩ, CL = 0.01 µF and RL = 1 kΩ.

circuits.title: Circuit for astable operation
circuits.description: Free-running oscillator. TRIG and THRES both watch the capacitor, so the timer retriggers itself: C fills through RA in series with RB up to two thirds of VCC, then discharges through RB into DISCH down to one third of VCC. The output is high for 0.693 × (RA + RB) × C and low for 0.693 × RB × C. RESET is tied to VCC; CONT carries an optional 0.01 µF capacitor to ground or is left open.

parts.note: CONT decoupling, or CONT left open

notes: Typical astable waveforms are given for RA = 5 kΩ, RB = 3 kΩ, C = 0.15 µF and RL = 1 kΩ.
A capacitor from CONT to ground can improve operation; whether it helps depends on the application.

circuits.title: Circuit for missing-pulse detector
circuits.description: Watchdog for a pulse train. Each input pulse drives TRIG and also turns on the PNP transistor, which empties the timing capacitor, so the monostable keeps restarting and the output stays high while the pulse spacing is under one interval. A missing pulse, a long gap or a stopped train lets C reach the threshold, and the output goes low.
notes: Completed-timing waveforms are given for VCC = 5 V, RA = 1 kΩ and C = 0.1 µF.

circuits.title: Frequency divider (divide by three)
circuits.description: The monostable circuit with its interval set longer than two input periods. Trigger edges that arrive while a pulse is running are ignored, so the output gives one pulse for every third input pulse.
notes: Same wiring as the monostable circuit; it divides by three with VCC = 5 V, RA = 1250 Ω and C = 0.02 µF.

circuits.title: Circuit for pulse-width modulation
circuits.description: Clock pulses start the monostable while a signal on CONT moves the threshold level, so each output pulse is as long as the modulating voltage asks: higher CONT voltage, longer pulse. Any modulating wave shape works.
notes: Pulse-width-modulation waveforms are given for RA = 3 kΩ, C = 0.02 µF and RL = 1 kΩ with sine-wave modulation.
The modulation may be coupled to CONT directly or through a capacitor; with direct coupling, the source's voltage and impedance shift the timer's bias.

circuits.title: Circuit for pulse-position modulation
circuits.description: The astable oscillator with a modulating signal on CONT. Moving the threshold level changes how long each charge takes, so the timing of every output pulse follows the modulation.
notes: Pulse-position-modulation waveforms are given for RA = 3 kΩ, RB = 500 Ω and RL = 1 kΩ with triangle-wave modulation.
The modulation may be coupled to CONT directly or through a capacitor; with direct coupling, the source's voltage and impedance shift the timer's bias.

circuits.title: Sequential timer circuit
circuits.description: Three monostables in a chain. Closing S for a moment starts timer A; when its output falls, the 0.001 µF capacitor and 33 kΩ pull-up give timer B a short trigger pulse, and B's falling output starts C the same way. Outputs A, B and C go high one after another, each for 1.1 × R × C of its own stage.
notes: Pulse lengths: twA = 1.1 RA CA, twB = 1.1 RB CB, twC = 1.1 RC CC. S closes momentarily at t = 0.

where.RA: timing resistor from VCC to DISCH and THRES

where.RB: resistor from DISCH to THRES and TRIG

equations.expr: twA = 1.1 × RA × CA; twB = 1.1 × RB × CB; twC = 1.1 × RC × CC

where.twA, twB, twC: pulse lengths of outputs A, B and C

operation.text: A timer that makes time delays (monostable) or oscillates (astable), over intervals from microseconds to hours. A monostable interval is set by one resistor and one capacitor; an astable uses two resistors and one capacitor, which set frequency and duty cycle separately.

An internal divider puts the threshold level at two thirds of VCC and the trigger level at one third. Both move when CONT is driven. TRIG falling below its level sets the latch and the output goes high; with TRIG above its level, THRES rising above its level resets the latch and the output goes low. While the output is low, DISCH is a low-impedance path to ground.
RESET overrides TRIG, and TRIG overrides THRES. RESET low resets the latch and the output goes low whatever the other inputs do; RESET can start a fresh timing cycle.
The output sinks or sources up to 200 mA (absolute maximum ±225 mA). Operation is specified at supplies of 5 V to 15 V; at VCC = 5 V the output levels suit TTL inputs.

A falling trigger sets the output high and releases the capacitor. TRIG must return high no later than 10 µs before the interval would end, or the cycle does not end. With TRIG held at ground, comparator storage time reaches up to 10 µs, so the shortest monostable pulse is 10 µs. Threshold levels and charging rate both scale with VCC, so the interval does not depend on supply voltage as long as VCC stays constant during the interval.

A low pulse applied to RESET and TRIG together during an interval discharges C; the new interval starts on the rising edge of the reset pulse, and the output stays low while RESET is low. An unused RESET goes to VCC to avoid false triggering.

With TRIG joined to THRES and a second resistor RB between DISCH and the capacitor, the timer runs freely: C charges through RA plus RB and discharges through RB alone, swinging between about 0.67 × VCC and 0.33 × VCC. RA and RB set the duty cycle; frequency and duty cycle do not depend on supply voltage. A capacitor from CONT to ground can improve operation.
THRES input current limits the total timing resistance: RA + RB up to about 3.4 MΩ at VCC = 5 V and 10 MΩ at VCC = 15 V.

While incoming pulses come closer together than the interval, each one restarts the monostable. A longer gap, a missing pulse or the end of the train lets the interval finish and produces an output pulse.

A monostable cannot be retriggered while its interval is running, so setting the interval to span several input periods divides the input frequency; with VCC = 5 V, RA = 1250 Ω and C = 0.02 µF it divides by three.

A voltage or current applied to CONT shifts the internal threshold and trigger levels. In a triggered monostable this modulates pulse width; in a free-running astable it modulates pulse position. Any modulating wave shape can be used. The signal can reach CONT directly or through a capacitor; when direct, its source voltage and impedance affect the timer's bias.
Timers can be chained, astable or monostable, with or without modulation, to give signals in sequence, for example initialization at start-up or ordered test signals.
NE555 is rated 0 °C to 70 °C, SA555 -40 °C to 85 °C, NA555 -40 °C to 105 °C, SE555 -55 °C to 125 °C. SE555 may run from supplies up to 18 V. Typical curves outside 0 °C to 70 °C apply to SE555 only.
